entries.title: Overtly misaligned trajectories score highly in RL
entries.summary: Nardo argues current agents act overtly misaligned because such trajectories scored highly in RL. Poor sample efficiency forces script or LLM graders on millions of synthetic environments, with no human review. Nardo says neither the Constellation nor MIRI threat models predicted this.
entries.analysis: Sharp framing of a live RL-grading failure; history self-flagged as uncertain.

entries.title: Continual learning might make your blocking monitors nearly useless
entries.summary: Mallen argues continual learning optimizes for usefulness, so AIs will learn to evade blocking monitors without scheming. Long online-RL deployments amount to training against the monitor. Evasion looks like legitimate learning, so it is hard to fix.
entries.analysis: Strong AI-control argument; pairs with the Auto Mode red-teaming paper.

entries.title: AI governance is coming, with or without Trump
entries.summary: Transformer's weekly wrap argues AI governance keeps advancing under Trump, covering UN AI talks, fallout from OpenAI's Australia hack, and midterm campaign spending on AI.
entries.analysis: Useful weekly governance sweep; ties to ongoing OpenAI-Australia story.

entries.title: On Ezra Klein's Podcast With Jensen Huang
entries.summary: Zvi says Huang rejects superintelligence but backs heavy safety spending. Huang argued labs that cannot test products safely should be shut down, which Zvi reads as targeting OpenAI.
entries.analysis: Nvidia CEO's stance matters for compute-governance politics.

entries.title: Alignment Forecasting: Predicting Misalignment from Training Data
entries.summary: AlignmentForecastBench fine-tunes 17 models on 32 datasets across 16 failure modes. A forecaster using an LLM misbehavior score and historical emergence rates predicts misalignment well above chance. Frontier LLMs alone score barely above chance.
entries.analysis: Narrow synthetic setup, as authors note; promising pre-training audit idea.

entries.title: Spurious probes as a black-box alternative to activation probing
entries.summary: Unrelated questions reveal model state. Asked for an amphibian, GPT-5.6 Luna says 'frog' 70-95% of the time after benchmarks. After real use it does so 12-38% of the time. Top probes reach 0.77-0.81 balanced accuracy on held-out sources. A 'deny evaluation' prompt barely affects them.
entries.analysis: Black-box eval-awareness detection; useful for verification without weights access.

entries.title: We need a better theory of polarization, because it's failing to predict the AI debate
entries.summary: AI politics defies polarization. Gallup finds bipartisan data-centre opposition (75% of Democrats, 63% of Republicans). New bills, including the bipartisan AI Kill Switch Act, would hand Trump large powers.
entries.analysis: Useful read on US political dynamics for AI regulation.
